fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: When a crown, inlay or onlay comes loose, the tooth underneath can feel sensitive, sharp or unfamiliar. While it is not always painful, a missing restoration leaves the tooth vulnerable to damage and decay. At Precision Dental, we can assess the tooth promptly and discuss whether your restoration can be re-cemented or needs replacing.

sections.label: What Are Crowns, Inlays and Onlays?

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Are Crowns, Inlays and Onlays?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A crown is a cap that covers the entire visible part of a tooth. An inlay fits within the grooves of a back tooth's chewing surface, while an onlay extends to cover one or more of the tooth's cusps. All three are custom-made restorations bonded or cemented to the tooth.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Restorations can come loose for several reasons, including decay developing beneath them, wear of the cement over time, biting on hard or sticky foods, grinding, or a fracture of the underlying tooth.

sections.label: What to Do Before Your Appointment

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What to Do Before Your Appointment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Keep the restoration safe in a small container and bring it with you. Gently clean the tooth by brushing, and avoid chewing on that side. A small amount of dental wax or temporary dental cement from a pharmacy can protect a sensitive tooth for a short time, but do not use household glue. Avoid sticky, hard or very hot or cold foods.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Happens at Your Appointment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We examine the tooth and your restoration and take digital X-rays to check for decay or fractures beneath it. If the tooth and restoration are both in good condition, we clean them and re-cement the restoration in place. If there is decay, damage, or the restoration no longer fits well, a replacement may be needed. With our CEREC system, many new crowns, inlays and onlays can be designed, milled and fitted during one visit. If the tooth is severely damaged, we explain other options, such as root canal therapy or replacement of the tooth.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Aftercare and Ongoing Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Avoid chewing on the tooth until any anaesthetic has worn off, and avoid sticky or very hard foods for the first 24 hours. Brush and clean between your teeth carefully around the restoration each day. If you grind your teeth, a night splint may help protect your restorations. Regular check-ups help us monitor restoration edges for early signs of decay or wear.

sections.label: Why Choose Precision Dental for a Lost Restoration

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Why Choose Precision Dental for a Lost Restoration

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Our in-house CEREC technology means many replacement restorations can be completed in a single visit, without a temporary. We assess the tooth carefully so the restoration is placed on a healthy foundation.

sections.label: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The cost of your treatment depends on your individual needs. After your examination, we talk you through your options and the expected fees before any treatment begins. We accept most major health funds, process claims on the spot through HICAPS and are a preferred provider for {{site:preferredFunds}}. Interest-free payment plans are available through DentiCare for eligible patients, subject to terms and conditions. You can learn more on our Prices and Payment Options page.

fields.label: Small label
fields.value: FAQ

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently Asked Questions

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can my old crown be put back on?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Often, yes, if the crown and the tooth underneath are in good condition. We will check both before re-cementing it.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: What if I swallowed my crown?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Swallowed restorations usually pass without harm. If you have difficulty breathing or coughing, seek medical care immediately. We can make a replacement.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can I glue my crown back on myself?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Please do not use household glue, as it can damage the tooth and make proper repair difficult. A temporary pharmacy cement may be used briefly.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Why did my crown fall out?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Common causes include decay beneath the crown, worn cement, biting on sticky foods and grinding.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Is a lost crown an emergency?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: It is not always urgent, but the tooth is vulnerable without it. It is best to be seen within a day or two, or sooner if you have pain.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can a lost onlay be replaced on the same day?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: In many cases, yes. Our CEREC system allows many onlays to be made and fitted in a single appointment.
